entries.name: setup
entries.summary: Runs once when the program starts, before the first tick.
entries.description: Define it as a global. Choose the screen mode, apply assets and set up state here. A Lua error in setup() ends the program before it ticks (the launcher gets nil, err).

entries.name: tick
entries.summary: Runs repeatedly, as often as the scheduler can, after setup().
entries.description: There are no arguments: read TimeNow() for elapsed time or WaitVSync() to pace to the display. Input arrives through InputPoll()/InputControl() or the on_keypress/on_control callbacks, which the scheduler runs between ticks. A due timer callback runs instead of the tick for that step; ticks and timer callbacks never overlap. A Lua error in tick() ends the program.
entries.example:
function tick()
    local frames = WaitVSync()
    if frames > 0 then update(frames) end
end

entries.name: finish
entries.summary: Runs once when the program exits, by ExitProgram() or an error.
entries.description: Video, audio and timers are released by the OS afterwards; use finish() to save state to the card.

entries.name: on_keypress
entries.signature: function on_keypress(key, shift, ctrl, cbm, restore)
entries.summary: Optional callback for key-down events.
entries.description: Called by the scheduler before the next tick for each key press (releases and modifier-only events are only visible through InputPoll). Looked up by name for every event, so it can be defined, replaced or removed at any time, including from setup(); the Input framework's Input.Keyboard.Callback installs one for you.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: ASCII code, or 128-140 for cursor/function keys (see Input.KEY_*)

entries.name: on_control
entries.signature: function on_control(index, up, down, left, right, fire)
entries.summary: Optional callback for joystick changes, with the full state.
entries.description: Called for every change on either joystick; index is 0 for joystick 1 and 1 for joystick 2. Looked up by name per event like on_keypress.

entries.name: args
entries.summary: The launch arguments as an array of strings.
entries.description: args[1] is the first word typed after the program name in the shell (also the chunk's first vararg); #args is the count. The shell turns a relative first argument into a /data path.

entries.name: app
entries.summary: Paths of the app bundle the program was launched from.
entries.description: A table with app.program (the file that was run), app.root (the bundle folder), app.resources (root/resources), app.metadata (root/app.json) and app.cwd. For a loose .prg the root is its folder.

entries.name: pid
entries.summary: This program's process id (also returned by Pid()).

entries.name: ApplyAssets
entries.summary: Applies the project's tile, palette, sound and score assets.
entries.description: Generated by the IDE for projects with asset components; the starter setup() calls it. Safe to call again to restore assets after another program ran.

entries.name: TimeNow
entries.summary: Milliseconds since boot (monotonic).
entries.example:
local t0 = TimeNow()
-- ...
local ms = TimeNow() - t0

entries.name: Pid
entries.summary: This program's process id.

entries.name: ExitProgram
entries.summary: Asks the OS to end the program after the current tick or callback returns.
entries.description: finish() runs, then the parent program resumes. If nothing is left on the program stack (a game, or the shell) the device restarts.

entries.name: Launch
entries.summary: Starts another program on top of this one, which pauses until it exits.
entries.description: The new program gets `arg` as args[1]. With replace = true the caller leaves the program stack instead: its state is released once this call returns (its remaining screen calls are ignored), and the new program's parent becomes the caller's parent. Boot uses replace to hand over to the shell; the shell uses it for games. Fails from mode 10 (nil, err).

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: program file: .prg or .lua, or an app bundle's app.prg

parameters.name: replace
parameters.description: take the caller's place on the stack

entries.name: Execute
entries.summary: Runs a program in the foreground with up to 16 string arguments; the caller pauses until it exits.
entries.description: Like Launch without replace, but with a full argument list (the program sees them as args). A utility's result arrives later through UtilityPoll().

entries.name: ExecuteString
entries.summary: Compiles and runs a Lua source string as a program in the foreground.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Lua source of a whole program (setup/tick)

entries.name: Compile
entries.summary: Compiles a Lua source file on the card into a .prg binary chunk.
entries.description: Same output as the IDE's build: parsed by the OS's own Lua in a scratch state (outside the caller's heap cap), debug info kept, chunk named after the source. dst defaults to src with .lua replaced by .prg. The shell's COMPILE command wraps it.

entries.name: UtilityResult
entries.summary: Ends the program, handing a result to the program that ran it.
entries.description: A utility always ends this way; an interactive program may too (a picker returning the user's choice). `value` is a string or a table; a table crosses into the caller's state with strings, numbers, booleans and nested tables (anything else becomes nil; 8 KB cap). The shell prints a table's `message` first, then its `lines` array in order, then every other field as KEY = VALUE; a table with a `run` path (and `kind`, `args`) makes the shell run that program instead, which is how the APPS launcher starts a game.

entries.name: UtilityPoll
entries.summary: Collects a finished utility's result, once.
entries.description: Returns the result of a child that ended with UtilityResult (a utility, or an interactive program that chose to), once, after the child exits; a table is rebuilt in the caller's state. A child that simply exits leaves nothing to collect (a utility that exits without a result reports that as an error).
entries.returns: ok, value (string or table), or nil when nothing is waiting
entries.example:
local ok, result = UtilityPoll()
if ok ~= nil then print(result.message) end

entries.name: TimerCreate
entries.summary: Starts an OS timer calling fn every interval_ms (or once).
entries.description: Callbacks take no arguments and run from the scheduler between ticks. At most 8 timers per program; 1 ms minimum. Timers pause while the program is paused by a launch. The Timer framework builds pausable timer objects on this.

parameters.name: oneshot
parameters.description: fire once, then release the timer

entries.name: TimerStop
entries.summary: Stops an OS timer.

entries.name: InputPoll
entries.summary: The next input event, or nil.
entries.description: Events queue while the program runs (128 deep, oldest dropped) and stay available even when callbacks are also defined. Releases and modifier keys are only visible here.
entries.returns: table {type = "key"|"control1"|"control2", key, mods, pressed, ctrl, dirs} or nil
entries.example:
while true do
    local ev = InputPoll()
    if not ev then break end
    if ev.type == "key" and ev.pressed == 1 then handle(ev.key) end
end

entries.name: InputControl
entries.summary: The current state of joystick n (1 or 2).
entries.returns: table {up, down, left, right, fire} of booleans, or nil
entries.example:
local j = InputControl(1)
if j and j.fire then shoot() end

entries.name: WaitVSync
entries.summary: Blocks until the display finishes a frame; returns frames elapsed since the previous call.
entries.description: Paces a game loop to 60 Hz. Without ms it gives up after about six frames so a stalled display cannot hang the program. WaitVSync(0) just reports the frames elapsed.
entries.returns: number of frames since this program's previous call
entries.example:
function tick()
    local n = WaitVSync()
    x = x + speed * n
end

entries.name: ScreenMode
entries.summary: Selects a screen mode; switching clears both layers.
entries.description: 0 = 40x30 tiles B&W, 1 = 40x30 tiles with per-cell invert and 7 colours, 2 = 80x60 tiles B&W, 3 = 80x60 tiles in colour (both at the full 640x480, 8x8 cells drawn 1:1), 10 = 320x240 pixels, 11 = 160x120 pixels (each shown 4x4), both one palette byte per pixel (one pixel-mode program at a time; Launch from a pixel mode fails). Cell and pixel coordinates in every other call are checked against the mode selected. The RP2040 dev board has modes 0 and 1 only.

entries.name: ScreenOut
entries.summary: Writes one character code to a cell of the base layer.
entries.description: x is 0-39, y 0-29, char 0-255 (tile index = character code; see the ROM character set in lua.md). Attribute byte: bit 7 inverts, bits 0-2 pick colour c, which uses palette entry c+1.

entries.name: ScreenAttr
entries.summary: Sets a cell's attribute, keeping its character.

entries.name: ScreenDefineTile
entries.summary: Redefines a character's 8x8 tile.
entries.description: bytes is a table of 8 row bytes or an 8-byte string; bit 0 of a row is the leftmost pixel (the ROM font's convention). The definition is part of the program's screen state and is restored when it resumes.

entries.name: ScreenPalette
entries.summary: Sets palette entry i (0-255) to an RGB colour.
entries.description: Entry 0 is the background, entry 1 the default text colour, entries 2-8 the seven attribute colours; mode 10 uses all 256.

entries.name: ScreenPaletteSet
entries.summary: Sets palette entries from an array of {r, g, b} tables or 0xRRGGBB numbers.

entries.name: ScreenClear
entries.summary: Fills the base layer with a character (default space) and attribute 0.

entries.name: ScreenBox
entries.signature: ScreenBox(x, y, w, h [, style [, attr]])
entries.summary: Draws a frame with the ROM box-drawing glyphs; one display op.
entries.description: style 1 = single line (default), 2 = double. Needs w and h >= 2; clipped at the screen edge. The inside is untouched.

entries.name: ScreenFill
entries.signature: ScreenFill(x, y, w, h [, char [, attr]])
entries.summary: Writes one character and attribute into every cell of a rectangle; one display op.

entries.name: ScreenFillAttr
entries.summary: Sets the attribute of every cell in a rectangle, characters unchanged; one display op.

entries.name: ScreenWrite
entries.summary: Writes a string as consecutive cells from (x, y), wrapping to the next row; one display op however long.
entries.description: A 1200-byte string at (0, 0) replaces the whole screen. With attr, every cell gets that attribute too.

entries.name: ScreenWriteAttr
entries.summary: The bytes of attrs become the attributes of consecutive cells from (x, y).

entries.name: ScreenCopy
entries.signature: ScreenCopy(sx, sy, w, h, dx, dy)
entries.summary: Copies a block (characters and attributes) so its top-left lands at (dx, dy); one display op.
entries.description: Clipped so both rectangles fit; overlapping copies are safe.

entries.name: ScreenMove
entries.signature: ScreenMove(sx, sy, w, h, dx, dy [, char [, attr]])
entries.summary: Moves a block, blanking what it uncovers with char and attr.

entries.name: ScreenScroll
entries.signature: ScreenScroll(x, y, w, h, dx, dy [, char [, attr]])
entries.summary: Shifts a region's contents by (dx, dy) cells; uncovered cells are filled.
entries.description: Negative dx/dy scroll left/up. One display op.
entries.example: ScreenScroll(0, 0, 40, 30, 0, -1) -- scroll the screen up one row

entries.name: ScreenLoadImage
entries.summary: Reserved: draws an image file at (x, y). Not implemented yet.
entries.description: Always returns nil and a message for now; the framework's Screen.LoadImage wraps it so programs can be written against the interface.

entries.name: ScreenPlot
entries.summary: Sets one pixel in mode 10 (320x240) or 11 (160x120) to a palette index.
entries.description: One display op per pixel: fine for a few, slow for animation; the other pixel calls (ScreenPixelRect, ScreenPixelLine, ScreenPixelCircle, ScreenBlit, ScreenPixelText, ScreenPixelScroll) and the Graphics framework draw whole shapes in one op.

entries.name: ScreenPixelRect
entries.signature: ScreenPixelRect(x, y, w, h, colour [, filled])
entries.summary: A rectangle outline (or filled) in the pixel modes, one op.
entries.description: Modes 10 and 11. Clipped by the display core, so it may run off the edges.

entries.name: ScreenPixelLine
entries.summary: A straight line of pixels between two points, one op.
entries.description: Modes 10 and 11; both ends included; clipped by the display core.

entries.name: ScreenPixelCircle
entries.summary: A circle outline (or filled) in the pixel modes, one op.
entries.description: Modes 10 and 11; radius 0-1024; clipped by the display core.

entries.name: ScreenPixelScroll
entries.signature: ScreenPixelScroll(x, y, w, h, dx, dy [, fill])
entries.summary: Shifts a rectangle of pixels by (dx, dy); uncovered pixels get fill.
entries.description: Modes 10 and 11; dx and dy -127..127; the region is clipped to the screen first. One op however large the region.

entries.name: ScreenBlit
entries.signature: ScreenBlit(x, y, w, h, pixels [, key])
entries.summary: Copies a w x h image of palette bytes to (x, y), optionally with a transparent colour.
entries.description: Modes 10 and 11. `pixels` holds w*h bytes row by row; with `key` pixels of that colour are skipped, which is how sprites keep their shape. Clipped at every edge. At most 8184 pixels per call (the Graphics framework splits larger images); the bytes travel through the 8 KB text staging ring.

entries.name: ScreenPixelText
entries.signature: ScreenPixelText(x, y, text, colour [, bg [, scale]])
entries.summary: Text as pixels with the 8x8 font in the pixel modes, one op.
entries.description: Modes 10 and 11. Each character is 8 * scale pixels wide and high (scale 1-4); with `bg` each character's cell is painted first, otherwise only the lit pixels are drawn. Uses the program's own tiles where defined. Up to 64 characters a call.

entries.name: OverlayOut
entries.summary: Writes one character to the overlay layer (the cell becomes visible).
entries.description: The overlay is one layer composited over the base: cells you write show, untouched cells stay transparent, OverlayClear hides everything. Dialogs and menus go here so the base screen survives underneath.

entries.name: OverlayAttr
entries.summary: Sets an overlay cell's attribute; bit 6 set makes it transparent again.
entries.description: The overlay is one layer composited over the base: cells you write show, untouched cells stay transparent, OverlayClear hides everything. Dialogs and menus go here so the base screen survives underneath.

entries.name: OverlayClear
entries.summary: Hides the whole overlay: every cell transparent again.
entries.description: The overlay is one layer composited over the base: cells you write show, untouched cells stay transparent, OverlayClear hides everything. Dialogs and menus go here so the base screen survives underneath.

entries.name: OverlayBox
entries.signature: OverlayBox(x, y, w, h [, style [, attr]])
entries.summary: Frame on the overlay; as ScreenBox.
entries.description: The overlay is one layer composited over the base: cells you write show, untouched cells stay transparent, OverlayClear hides everything. Dialogs and menus go here so the base screen survives underneath.

entries.name: OverlayFill
entries.signature: OverlayFill(x, y, w, h [, char [, attr]])
entries.summary: Rectangle fill on the overlay; as ScreenFill.
entries.description: The overlay is one layer composited over the base: cells you write show, untouched cells stay transparent, OverlayClear hides everything. Dialogs and menus go here so the base screen survives underneath.

entries.name: OverlayFillAttr
entries.summary: Attribute fill on the overlay; as ScreenFillAttr.
entries.description: The overlay is one layer composited over the base: cells you write show, untouched cells stay transparent, OverlayClear hides everything. Dialogs and menus go here so the base screen survives underneath.

entries.name: OverlayCopy
entries.signature: OverlayCopy(sx, sy, w, h, dx, dy)
entries.summary: Block copy on the overlay; as ScreenCopy.
entries.description: The overlay is one layer composited over the base: cells you write show, untouched cells stay transparent, OverlayClear hides everything. Dialogs and menus go here so the base screen survives underneath.

entries.name: OverlayMove
entries.signature: OverlayMove(sx, sy, w, h, dx, dy [, char [, attr]])
entries.summary: Block move on the overlay; as ScreenMove (fill with attr 0x40 to leave transparency).
entries.description: The overlay is one layer composited over the base: cells you write show, untouched cells stay transparent, OverlayClear hides everything. Dialogs and menus go here so the base screen survives underneath.

entries.name: OverlayScroll
entries.signature: OverlayScroll(x, y, w, h, dx, dy [, char [, attr]])
entries.summary: Region scroll on the overlay; as ScreenScroll.
entries.description: The overlay is one layer composited over the base: cells you write show, untouched cells stay transparent, OverlayClear hides everything. Dialogs and menus go here so the base screen survives underneath.

entries.name: OverlayWrite
entries.summary: String write on the overlay; as ScreenWrite.
entries.description: The overlay is one layer composited over the base: cells you write show, untouched cells stay transparent, OverlayClear hides everything. Dialogs and menus go here so the base screen survives underneath.

entries.name: OverlayWriteAttr
entries.summary: Attribute bytes on the overlay; as ScreenWriteAttr.
entries.description: The overlay is one layer composited over the base: cells you write show, untouched cells stay transparent, OverlayClear hides everything. Dialogs and menus go here so the base screen survives underneath.

entries.name: SoundDefine
entries.summary: Defines instrument id (0-31) from a spec table.
entries.description: spec = {base = "built-in name" (start from that sound; the other fields override), wave = "square"|"pulse"|"triangle"|"saw"|"sine"|"noise", duty = 1..15, attack = ms, decay = ms, sustain = 0..255, release = ms, volume = 0..255, note = "C5" (the sound's own pitch), slide = semitones per second (a laser is -300, a jump +180), vibrato = cents with vibrato_rate = Hz, arp/arp2 = semitone steps every arp_ms ms (arp_loop = true cycles them: a coin is arp 7 after 60 ms), cutoff = 0..255 (255 open, lower darker)}; every field is optional.
entries.example:
SoundDefine(0, { base = "laser", slide = -900 })
SoundDefine(1, { wave = "triangle", attack = 5, decay = 80, sustain = 100, release = 60 })

entries.name: SoundPreset
entries.summary: A built-in sound's id and its definition as a spec table.
entries.description: The bank has instruments (lead, pulse, bass, piano, organ, strings, flute, brass, bell, pluck, chime, kick, snare, hihat, tom, clap) and effects (coin, jump, laser, zap, explosion, hit, hurt, powerup, blip, select, error, alarm, engine, splash, bounce, teleport). The id (64 + index) plays with SoundPlay and in scores; the spec can be changed and given to SoundDefine under an id of your own.
entries.example:
local id, spec = SoundPreset("laser")
spec.slide = -900
SoundDefine(0, spec)

entries.name: SoundPresets
entries.summary: Lists the built-in sounds: { name, effect, id } each, in bank order.
entries.description: `effect` is true for the sound effects (played at their own pitch) and false for the instruments (played at the note you give).
entries.returns: an array of { name =, effect =, id = }
entries.example: for _, p in ipairs(SoundPresets()) do print(p.name, p.effect) end

entries.name: SoundLoad
entries.summary: Loads a WAV file (8/16-bit PCM, mono/stereo, <= 48 kHz) into the program's 64 KB sample pool.
entries.description: `root` is the note the recording is of (a name or MIDI number, default C4): playing the sample at another note resamples it by the difference, so one recording of a bass at C2 plays the whole scale (an octave up doubles the rate, so keep large shifts to drums and effects where the change of character is welcome). The sample is an instrument for SoundPlay and scores, ids 32-39.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: a WAV file on the card

parameters.name: loop_start
parameters.description: first frame of the sustain loop

parameters.name: loop_end
parameters.description: frame after the loop; the note repeats the stretch until released

entries.returns: sound id usable with SoundPlay and in scores, or nil, err

entries.name: SoundPlay
entries.summary: Plays a sound: a built-in name or an id, at a note, for a length.
entries.description: `sound` is the name of a built-in sound ("coin", "piano", ... see SoundPresets), an id from SoundDefine (0-31) or SoundLoad (32-39). `note` is a MIDI number or a name ("C4"); without one the sound's own note is used (effects carry theirs), else C4. `dur_ms` 0 or absent plays the sound's own envelope. Returns the one-shot voice (1-8) or nil, err when none is free.
entries.returns: voice id, or nil, err when no voice is free

entries.name: SoundStop
entries.summary: Releases one voice returned by SoundPlay.

entries.name: SoundStopAll
entries.summary: Releases every one-shot voice.

entries.name: SoundVolume
entries.summary: Sets the master volume 0-255.

entries.name: SoundSpectrum
entries.summary: Ten band levels (0..255) of everything playing, a decaying peak per band from 60 Hz to 4 kHz; a table passed in is refilled.

parameters.name: t
parameters.description: a list from a previous call to refill (optional)

entries.name: SoundSpectrumBands
entries.summary: The centre frequency in Hz of each SoundSpectrum band.

entries.name: MusicDefine
entries.summary: Defines a score: channels of note events, played by name.
entries.description: spec = {loop = bool, length = ms, channels = { { {time, sound, note, dur, vol, pan}, ... }, ... } } with up to 8 channels and 1024 events per program. Scores live outside the Lua heap.

entries.name: MusicPlay
entries.summary: Starts a defined score; loop overrides the score's own flag.

entries.name: MusicStop
entries.summary: Stops the playing score.

entries.name: MusicPlaying
entries.summary: True while a score plays.

entries.name: ModLoad
entries.summary: Loads a ProTracker .mod (4 channels, 31 samples) from the card, streamed as it plays.
entries.description: One module per program (a second load replaces the first). The header, order list and two patterns are kept; samples up to a 48 KB resident budget stay in RAM (shortest first) and the rest keep a 2 KB head and stream through 8 KB per-channel rings that the OS core refills from the card between scheduler steps (a loop streams round without a break; one that fits the ring is kept there), about 82 KB in all, leaving the program around 65 KB of Lua heap on the device. 15-sample Soundtracker modules load too; 6/8-channel ones are refused. Very sample-heavy modules may not stream fast enough (ModInfo reports underruns).

entries.name: ModPlay
entries.summary: Plays the loaded module from the top (looping unless loop is false); a playing score stops.

entries.name: ModStop
entries.summary: Stops the module.

entries.name: ModPlaying
entries.summary: True while the module plays.
entries.example: if not ModPlaying() then ModPlay() end

entries.name: ModPosition
entries.summary: The player's order, row and pattern, to sync a game to the music.

entries.name: ModInfo
entries.summary: The loaded module's name, orders, patterns, samples, resident KB and underruns.

entries.name: ModChannels
entries.summary: The four channels' sample, note, period, volume (0..64), level (0..255) and active flag, for a tracker view; a table passed in is refilled.

parameters.name: t
parameters.description: a list from a previous call to refill (optional)

entries.returns: a list of four tables, or nil

entries.name: ModRows
entries.summary: Rows of a pattern in RAM (the playing one or the next) as strings of four "C-2 05 C40" cells; rows outside 0..63 are "".
entries.returns: a list of strings, or nil, err when the pattern is not resident
entries.example:
local _, row, pattern = ModPosition()
for _, line in ipairs(ModRows(pattern, row - 4, 9)) do print(line) end

entries.name: ModSamples
entries.summary: The module's 31 sample slots as { name, length, volume, loop }; an unused slot has length 0.
entries.returns: a list of 31 tables, or nil

entries.name: ModUnload
entries.summary: Stops and frees the loaded module.

entries.name: fs
entries.summary: The SD card module: files, folders and whole-file helpers.
entries.description: Paths are absolute (/data/notes.txt) or relative to the program's folder. The shell only lets its own commands touch /data; programs can read anywhere and should write under /data.

entries.name: fs.open
entries.summary: Opens a file and returns a file object.
entries.description: mode "r" (default), "w" (create/truncate), "a" (append), "r+"/"w+"/"a+". Up to 8 files open at once. Methods: read, write, seek, tell, size, flush, close.

entries.name: fs.ls
entries.summary: Lists a folder.
entries.description: Entries of a folder on the card, in directory order. A folder that does not exist (or cannot be opened) returns nil and an error message, not an empty list. Each entry is a table, so a very large folder costs heap: list it in a utility (the shell's DIR does) when memory is tight.
entries.returns: array of {name, size, dir} tables, or nil, err
entries.example: for _, e in ipairs(fs.ls("/data")) do print(e.name, e.size, e.dir) end

entries.name: fs.find
entries.summary: Finds an entry by name in a folder, case-insensitively.
entries.returns: the entry's actual name, or nil

entries.name: fs.stat
entries.summary: Information about a file or folder.
entries.example:
local info = fs.stat("/data/notes.txt")
if info and not info.dir then ... end

entries.name: fs.exists
entries.summary: True when the path exists.

entries.name: fs.mkdir
entries.summary: Creates a folder.

entries.name: fs.remove
entries.summary: Deletes a file or an empty folder.

entries.name: fs.rename
entries.summary: Renames or moves a file or folder.

entries.name: fs.free
entries.summary: Free and total space on the card, in KB.

entries.name: fs.ready
entries.summary: True while the card is mounted.

entries.name: fs.mount
entries.summary: Re-mounts the card (after a swap).

entries.name: fs.readall
entries.summary: Reads a whole file (128 KB cap).

entries.name: fs.writeall
entries.summary: Writes a whole file, creating or replacing it.

entries.name: :read
entries.summary: Reads up to n bytes from a file object.
entries.returns: string, or nil at end of file

entries.name: :write
entries.summary: Writes a string to a file object.

entries.name: :seek
entries.summary: Moves the file position; whence "set" (default), "cur" or "end".

entries.name: :tell
entries.summary: The current file position.

entries.name: :size
entries.summary: The file's size in bytes.

entries.name: :flush
entries.summary: Writes buffered data to the card.

entries.name: :close
entries.summary: Closes the file object (do this: only 8 can be open).

entries.name: dofile
entries.summary: Runs a Lua file from the card and returns what it returns.
entries.description: SD-backed; a .prg sibling is preferred over the .lua source.

entries.name: loadfile
entries.summary: Loads a Lua file from the card without running it.

entries.name: require
entries.summary: Loads a module from the card, once.
entries.description: Looks for NAME.prg, NAME.lua, /NAME(.prg/.lua) and /lib/NAME(.prg/.lua); compiled modules win. The result is cached in package.loaded.
